footnote: Source: 2025 and 2026 Government Work Reports, Ministry of Finance 2026 budget report (March 2026)
notes: The deficit ratio stays at about 4%, and the deficit rises by ¥230 billion to ¥5.89 trillion. Ultra-long special treasury bonds stay at ¥1.3 trillion and local government special bonds at ¥4.4 trillion. Special bonds to recapitalize the big state-owned banks fall from ¥500 billion to ¥300 billion. Added up, new government borrowing is ¥11.89 trillion, only ¥30 billion more than 2025's ¥11.86 trillion, so this is a slight step up rather than a big push. General budget spending passes ¥30 trillion for the first time. Within the ultra-long bonds, ¥800 billion goes to major strategic projects, ¥250 billion to consumer trade-ins (¥50 billion less than last year) and ¥200 billion to equipment upgrades. A new ¥100 billion fund pairs fiscal and financial tools to support domestic demand, and central budget investment is ¥755 billion.
